title: Human-Controlled AI Lab
summary: An interactive goal-to-plan workflow that makes interpretation, approval, rejection, failure, and fallback visible—applying the same experience-system grammar used for complex product UX to agentic interfaces.
role: Creative technologist — interaction model, structured-output contract, Nitro API, safety boundaries, and frontend
timeframe: August 2026 portfolio launch, building on design-system and complex-workflow patterns from prior product work
problem: Fuzzy prompts and autonomous actions can make AI feel fast but difficult to trust. The interface needs to turn hidden reasoning boundaries into understandable choices—the same requirement complex operational tools have for locks, dependencies, and recovery.
constraints: Ideas are limited to 240 characters and raw input is never sent to analytics.
The public experience must work without an API key or live quota.
Only explicit approval can trigger the final result.
The live flow is stateless and accepts read-only tools only.
Agent UX must inherit accessibility and reversible-action habits from the broader experience-systems practice, not invent a parallel grammar.
approach: Start with a deterministic replay so the complete interaction is always available.
Return an interpreted goal, no more than three steps, and exactly one pending action.
Use a signed continuation token instead of storing transcripts.
Treat reject, timeout, malformed output, missing credentials, and quota limits as named interface states with safe fallback—not silent failures.
Expose related public case studies through read-only tools so the agent can point to media, spatial, visualization, and UX proof without inventing claims.
Keep approve/reject keyboard-complete and visually distinct, matching the control clarity expected in complex product workflows.

evidence.label: Safety proof
evidence.value: HMAC continuation and anonymous quota cookies

evidence.label: Resilience proof
evidence.value: Replay fallback for credentials, quota, timeout, and model errors

evidence.label: Systems proof
evidence.value: Shared experience-system patterns: visible state, recovery, and an inspectable decision journal

evidence.label: Catalog proof
evidence.value: Read-only tools that resolve related public stories across media, spatial, visualization, and UX
